result.reason: The redline reaches the fallback position: it limits inspections to once per twelve-month period, retains 30 days’ notice (more protective than the fallback’s 15 days), confines inspection to business hours, and leaves all costs with HDI. It does not reach the preferred position because the inspection may be conducted by HDI’s General Manager rather than an independent, confidentiality-bound auditor, and it does not expressly prohibit direct systems access. The amendment is narrowly tailored and preserves the existing scope and cost allocation, though the inherited phrase “may ... have the right” is stylistically awkward.
